mission_05: FedProx addresses the instability of FedAvg in heterogeneous settings where clients have different data distributions and computational capabilities. The key innovation is adding a proximal term to the local objective: mu/2 * ||w - w_global||^2. This term penalizes local models that drift too far from the global model, acting as a stabilizing force. Unlike FedAvg which assumes all clients perform the same number of local steps, FedProx naturally handles system heterogeneity by allowing clients to train for different numbers of epochs. The proximal coefficient mu controls the trade-off: larger mu keeps local models closer to the global model (more stable but less personalized), while smaller mu allows more local adaptation. FedProx has been shown to converge under broader conditions than FedAvg in non-IID settings.
